facts.text: A headless simulation computes only the numbers a test needs without drawing pictures, whereas a rendered simulation produces images or sensor views at a much greater computing cost.
facts.quote: A headless simulation runs without drawing any picture, computing only the numbers a test needs, while a rendered simulation produces images or sensor views, which costs far more computing.

facts.text: An object-list braking-logic test can run without rendering, representing the machine as a point with a speed and the worker as a point with a position, and producing a stopping distance.
facts.quote: A braking-logic test with an object list does not need to see anything: the machine is a point with a speed, the worker is a point with a position, and the result is a stopping distance.

facts.text: Headless object-list braking-logic runs use ordinary processors, run far faster than real time, and can spread across thousands of cheap processor cores.
facts.quote: Such runs use ordinary processors, run far faster than real time and spread across thousands of cheap processor cores [Chapter 11].

facts.text: Rendering is needed only when a camera, lidar or radar model must receive a view of the scene; a graphics processing unit traces rays through geometry and materials, slowing the simulation toward real time or below.
facts.quote: Rendering is needed only when a camera, lidar or radar model must be fed with a view of the scene; then a graphics processing unit (GPU) traces rays through geometry and materials, and the run slows toward real time or below [Chapters 5, 11].

facts.text: Within the program's four-month window, tests per wall-clock hour matter more than real-time rendering.
facts.quote: in a four-month window, tests per wall-clock hour matter more than real-time rendering

facts.text: Lower-fidelity simulation models can screen the broad test space, while high-fidelity rendering should be reserved for perception-sensitive subsets.
facts.quote: lower-fidelity models can screen the broad space, and high-fidelity rendering is reserved for perception-sensitive subsets [Chapters 5, 11].

facts.text: Most of the millions of braking-logic combinations should run headless.
facts.quote: Most of the millions of braking-logic combinations should run headless

facts.text: Rendered simulation runs are a scarce, expensive resource and should be allocated to cases identified by correlation and sensitivity work.
facts.quote: rendered runs are the scarce, expensive resource to be spent on the cases that correlation and sensitivity work identify [Chapter 11].
